chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I heard him saying: 'Supplicate, and do not say that the matter has already been decided, for the supplication is worship.'
Indeed, God Mighty and Majestic says: 'Surely those who are too proud to worship Me shall soon enter Hell, abased.'
And He said: 'Call upon Me, I will answer you.'

key_terms.الدُّعَاء: Supplication (du'a) — the act of calling upon God; here defined as the very essence of worship
key_terms.الْعِبَادَة: Worship — the totality of devotional acts; equated with supplication to elevate its religious status
key_terms.دَاخِرِين: Abased/humiliated — the ultimate reversal for those who disdained submission
key_terms.عَزَّ وَجَلَّ: Mighty and Majestic — standard honorific for God emphasizing His power and transcendence

ai.seo_question: Is supplication (du'a) itself a form of worship in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) teaches that supplication (du'a) is not a futile act overridden by divine predetermination, but is itself the essence of worship. The Imam invokes two Quranic verses from Surah Ghafir (40:60) to establish both the grave consequence of abandoning du'a out of arrogance and the divine promise of response for those who call upon God. The original audience of early Shia Muslims would have understood this as a direct refutation of fatalistic attitudes that could paralyze religious practice.
